explanation: The Christian apostle who was a central figure in the spread of the gospel, here imprisoned on Malta after a shipwreck.
An island in the Mediterranean Sea where Paul was shipwrecked and where he healed many people during his stay.
A maritime disaster where a ship's crew was saved to land by swimming or using rafts, which happened to Paul on his way to Rome.
A venomous snakebite that struck Paul when he was gathering wood, but which caused him no harm.
The act where God restored health to sick people through Paul, including the father of the islanders and others on Malta.
The capital of the Roman Empire where Paul arrived to continue his ministry under house arrest.
The good news of salvation through Jesus Christ that Paul preached freely to all, both Jews and Gentiles.
